condition: Endoscopy antithrombotic management — apixaban before ERCP with sphincterotomy
summary: 76-year-old man on apixaban for AF with CBD stones (ASGE high risk, no cholangitis) booked for ERCP with sphincterotomy (high bleeding-risk procedure).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Booked for ERCP for bile duct stones — takes apixaban
inputs.hpi: Admitted last week with biliary colic and mild jaundice, now settled. MRCP: several 6–8 mm stones in an 11 mm CBD. No fever or rigors. Atrial fibrillation on apixaban 5 mg twice daily; no previous stroke. Booked for ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone extraction.

exam.general: Mildly icteric. Irregular pulse 78, BP 138/82, RR 14, SpO2 97% on air, T 36.7°C.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild RUQ tenderness, Murphy's sign negative.

imaging.name: MRCP
imaging.result: Several 6–8 mm filling defects in an 11 mm common bile duct. Gallbladder with small stones. Pancreas normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Choledocholithiasis — ERCP with sphincterotomy; apixaban for AF
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Choledocholithiasis, ASGE high risk, no cholangitis. ERCP with sphincterotomy (high bleeding-risk procedure). AF on apixaban — interrupt before ERCP, no bridging.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: inguinal hernia, cholecystitis, GORD. The 'Obstructive jaundice' CC template adds no features, the SOCRATES answers carry no jaundice words, and paneAnswers only set us_gallstones.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: Seed PANE jaundice/dark_urine features from the jaundice symptom chip and bilirubin result (the HPB cluster's PANE priors issue also applies: inguinal hernia prior 0.15).

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: BSG/ESGE guideline — endoscopy in patients on antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy (2021 update)
guideline.section: Low-risk procedures (diagnostic ± biopsy): continue P2Y12 inhibitors and warfarin (INR in the week before, within therapeutic range), omit the morning DOAC dose. High-risk procedures (polypectomy, EMR, ERCP with sphincterotomy): P2Y12 inhibitor stopped 7 days before when thrombotic risk is low; high thrombotic risk (coronary stents) — continue aspirin and liaise with the cardiologist about stopping the P2Y12 inhibitor; warfarin stopped 5 days before (INR <1.5), bridging only for high thrombotic risk; DOAC stopped before the procedure (interval by drug and renal function), no bridging
guideline.citation: Veitch AM, Radaelli F, Alikhan R, et al. Gut. 2021;70:1611–28.

guideline.name: PAUSE study — perioperative DOAC interruption without bridging or coagulation testing
guideline.section: Apixaban/rivaroxaban/edoxaban omitted 1 day before low-bleed-risk and 2 days before high-bleed-risk procedures (dabigatran longer when CrCl <50 mL/min), no bridging, no pre-operative coagulation tests
guideline.citation: Douketis JD, Spyropoulos AC, Duncan J, et al. JAMA Intern Med. 2019;179:1469–78.

guideline.name: ASGE guideline — choledocholithiasis
guideline.section: High risk (CBD stone on imaging, cholangitis, or bilirubin >4 mg/dL with dilated CBD) → ERCP
guideline.citation: Buxbaum JL, Abbas Fehmi SM, Sultan S, et al. Gastrointest Endosc. 2019;89:1075–105.

rationale: Permutation: DOAC before the high-risk ERCP sphincterotomy. Complements the existing warfarin vignette (choledocholithiasis-elderly-warfarin).
